chunks: Ahmad b. al-Hasan, known as Abu Ali b. Abduwayh, narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali al-Sukkari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Zakariyya al-Jawhari narrated to us. He said: al-Abbas ibn Bakkar narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn b. Yazid narrated to me from Umar b. Ali b. al-Husayn, from Fatima bint al-Husayn, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, from Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib.
She said: When al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was delivered from his mother's womb and I was attending to her, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: O aunt, bring my son to me.
So I said: O Messenger of God, we have not cleansed him yet.
He (peace be upon him and his family) said: O aunt, will you cleanse him?! Surely, God, blessed and exalted, has already cleansed and purified him.

key_terms.نظّفه وطهّره: Cleansed and purified him — indicating both physical and spiritual purity bestowed by God
key_terms.هلمي: Bring (imperative, feminine) — an Arabic command form expressing urgency
key_terms.وليتها: Attending to her, acting as midwife — Safiyya's role at the birth

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say when asked to wait for the newborn Husayn to be cleansed?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through a detailed chain of nine narrators including descendants of Imam al-Husayn, recounts the moments following the birth of Imam al-Husayn (AS). Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's paternal aunt and the midwife present at the birth, hesitated to bring the newborn before cleaning him. The Prophet's response — that God Himself had already cleansed and purified the child — reflects the Shia doctrine of the inherent purity of the Ahl al-Bayt, echoing the Quranic verse of purification (33:33).
